title: Why the screen did not update
cards/0/title: The screen does not watch the model on its own
cards/0/body: A binding does not poll the property every second. The model has to announce it: "my property changed." That is what the INotifyPropertyChanged interface and its PropertyChanged event are for.
cards/1/task: Code changes the name, but the screen does not budge. Fix the model and check.
cards/2/q: Why didn't the screen update without INotifyPropertyChanged?
cards/2/options/0: The model never raised PropertyChanged, so the binding never learned about the change
cards/3/body:
OneWay: from the model to the screen.
TwoWay: both directions (the default for TextBox.Text).
OneTime: once, at startup.
OneWayToSource: only from the screen to the model.
cards/4/task: Code updates the TextBox, but what the user types never reaches the model. Change the mode.
cards/5/task: Pick the mode in which both typing and changes from code show up everywhere.
cards/6/q: Match each mode to its direction
cards/7/q: Which line makes the screen update?
cards/7/explain: OnPropertyChanged raises the PropertyChanged event with the property name.
cards/8/q: The user typed some text, the model got it, but the greeting (a TextBlock bound to the same property) did not update. What is wrong?
cards/8/options/0: The model did not raise PropertyChanged, so other bindings to Name never heard about the change
cards/8/explain: That is exactly what the first exercise without INotifyPropertyChanged showed.
